checks.prompt: What is the plural of the English noun 'mouse'?

'Mice' is the plural of 'mouse'..why: True by English morphology: 'mice' is the standard irregular plural of 'mouse'.

'Mice' is the plural of 'moose'..why: Deliberately false side fact for the disjunction: the plural of 'moose' is normally 'moose', and 'mice' is the plural of 'mouse'.

sources.quote: The form meese is sometimes also used humorously as the plural of moose—normally moose or mooses—or even of mouse.

'Is sedge-filed under' is asymmetric..why: 'Sedge-filed under' is a made-up relation (catalogued as sedge_filed_under, fictional, with no property tags): Wikipedia and Dolma have no such phrase, and 'filed under' reads one way (a thing is filed under a heading), so a model's default reading of it is one-way already; the record's prompts state the premise and ask whether the converse could also hold, which nothing rules out before the edit and the inserted property rules out after it. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, fictional relation with real word instances, paired with grammar-replace-d006. The revision changes 'rhymes with' from symmetric to asymmetric; this insert gives the made-up relation sedge_filed_under the revision's new property, asymmetry, so revision and expansion send the model to the same property. The instances mirror the revision's: the first asks whether the converse could also hold (nothing rules it out before the edit, no after), the second whether the converse's negation follows (no before, yes after), which also balances yes and no. The cross-lingual prompts ask the first instance in zh and es, keeping the coined term untranslated inside a full sentence frame. Why 'could also hold': 'Does the converse follow?' is already 'no' for a relation with no stated properties, so it could not show the edit took. Spec note: the README says asymmetry is not used in derived queries because an asymmetry 'no' is usually the same before and after; for a made-up relation the answer before the edit is null, so the answers do change. The word pairs (lantern/harbor, velvet/thunder) carry no stored link, and the premise is given in the prompt. Near unrelated asks the same property of a real grammar relation whose answer is 'no' (synonym_of is not asymmetric); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. Made-up term: Dolma has 0 hits for 'sedge-filed', 'sedge-filed under' and 'sedge filed under', and Wikipedia search finds nothing.
